title: Cross-functional reliability activation kit - sprint plan & runbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, pragmatic activation kit for a cross-functional reliability program focused on SLO adoption for model-serving surfaces (hosted API + dedicated). Goal: move from ad-hoc reliability work to a repeatable 6-week playbook teams can run with Platform, SRE, and Product support.

Scope and constraints:
- Surface: inference traffic handled by hosted-api and dedicated clusters (not private on-prem installs).
- Pilot teams: chat-routing-service, embeddings-indexer, model-cache.
- Exclude: data-retention/compliance tasks (handled by security team separately).
- Assumes basic observability (metrics, traces, synthetics) already available.

Objectives (measurable):
1) Define and publish SLOs for pilot services within 3 weeks.
2) Implement dashboarding + automated alert rules (error budget burn, latency p95 breaches) by week 4.
3) Run one canary rollout with SLO guardrails and fallback policy by week 6.
4) Capture a reproducible runbook and handoff checklist for org-wide adoption.

SLO candidate set (examples to iterate):
- Request latency SLO: p95 < 120ms for short-request route (<=512 tokens).
- Availability SLO: Successful-response-rate >= 99.7% (5m rolling) for customer-tiered endpoints.
- Correctness/quality proxy: downstream rerate >= baseline (measured by prompt testset pass-rate >= 95%).
(Notes: quality SLO is a soft SLO during pilot; use eval harness from Optimize team.)

Signals & dashboards (minimum):
- Tokenized request rate by route, latency histograms, p50/p95/p99, queue length, node CPU/GPU utilization.
- Error rate broken down by class (timeouts, 5xx, model-step failures).
- KV cache hit rate, batching efficiency, cost-per-token estimate.
- Synthetic prompt set pass-rate and drift signal.
- Error budget burn chart + projected exhaustion timeline.

6-week sprint plan (high level):
Week 0 (kickoff):
- Workshop: align goals, onboard pilot teams, map owners. Create JIRA epic JIRA-PLAT-987.
- Inventory: list existing dashboards, alerts, playbooks.
Week 1: SLO definition sprint
- Draft SLOs per service. Document SLI definitions precisely (what counts as success).
- Quick review with Product and CS on user-impact mapping.
Week 2: Telemetry gap closure
- Instrument missing SLIs (tracing hooks, synthetic runners). Small infra PRs to add labels/tags.
Week 3: Dashboard + alerting
- Create SLO dashboards, error-budget burn alerts, and paging thresholds.
- Run tabletop on alert noise tuning.
Week 4: Runbook & rollback rules
- Draft runbook: on-call steps for p95 spikes, cache eviction, model fallback.
- Implement automated fallback policy (route to smaller model or regional fallback).
Week 5: Canary and experiment
- Canary rollout using canary cohorts + SLO monitoring. 48-72h guardrails.
- Document lessons; iterate thresholds.
Week 6: Handoff & templateization
- Finalize activation kit template, publish confluence page, record a 30-min walkthrough.

Roles & RACI (summary):
- Platform Eng (Aisha): owner for orchestration and fallback primitives (R).
- SRE: owner for dashboards, alerts, oncall response (A/R).
- Product: consult + accept SLOs (C).
- Solutions Eng / CS: C for customer-impact mapping and canary validation.
- Infra Eng: I for low-level GPU/node tuning.

Playbook artifacts to produce:
- SLO definition sheet (CSV/markdown) per service.
- Dashboard templates (Grafana links) and alert rules (PagerDuty runbook).
- Runbook doc: step-by-step triage + remediation checklist.
- Postmortem template adapted for SLO breaches.

Communications plan:
- Weekly 30m sync with pilot teams (Tue 10:30 AM PT).
- Mid-pilot demo + exec snapshot at week 4 for product & GTM.
- Confluence publish + slack #reliability-activation channel for async updates.

Decision points and escalation triggers:
- If error budget projection shows exhaustion < 72h -> immediate rollback and paging.
- If synthetic quality signal drops > 10% -> pause rollout and engage Research/Optimize.
- If canary fails twice for unrelated reasons -> escalate to PL and SRE lead for stop/go decision.

Risks & mitigations:
- Alert fatigue: tune thresholds early, use staged paging (paging after sustained burn).
- Incomplete SLIs: prioritize synthetic and latency instrumentation first.
- Model-quality regressions: keep automated evals gated and add quick rollback paths.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm metric ownership for batching efficiency (assign to serving-runtime).
- Decide default SLO targets for trial tenants vs enterprise tenants.
- Identify data-retention constraints for synthetic test logs.

Next steps (owner + due):
- Aisha: schedule kickoff + create JIRA epic (due 2026-07-20).
- Jonah: inventory dashboards & share links (due 2026-07-22).
- Marina: draft SLO definitions for chat-routing-service (due 2026-07-29).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a lightweight SLO linter CI step for PRs touching serving runtime (prevent regressions).
- Add a cost-sensitivity table to SLO docs showing tradeoffs (latency vs token-cost).

Appendix: quick links and templates:
- SLO definition template: docs/runbook-template-v2#slo-template
- Canary playbook checklist: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/canary-checklist
- Related tickets: JIRA-PLAT-987, JIRA-SLO-201, github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/432

End of draft activation kit. This is intentionally concise and iterative — the goal is a minimal runnable kit we can refine after pilot lessons.
